idiom_name: plain tagged objects ({ kind: 'circle', radius }) + switch
implementation_notes: JavaScript has neither a type system nor a sum type: variants are plain objects carrying a literal tag field, products are simply their other properties, and dispatch is a switch on the tag (or a handler lookup table). Nothing checks that a tag is handled or that the payload matches its tag; exhaustiveness exists only after the same objects are described to TypeScript or to checkJs as a discriminated union, so the guarantee lives in the tooling, not at runtime. Keep factory functions that build each variant so tag and payload cannot drift, and freeze the values if callers might mutate them.
pitfalls: No exhaustiveness: a new variant only reaches the default branch at run time, and a missing default silently returns undefined.
switch compares with strict equality, so a numeric tag decoded from JSON (1) never matches the string case ("1").
Nothing ties the tag to the payload - a hand-built object can claim kind: "circle" while carrying side; keep construction behind factory functions.
Objects are mutable, so a value can change variant in place; freeze them (or use a record-like library) to keep the value semantics.
